items.title: 의뢰 맡깁니다
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-123753 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. An unauthenticated caller could supply a non-anonymous WS-Addressing wsa:ReplyTo or wsa:FaultTo address, and Axis2 would open a connection to that address to deliver the response or fault, allowing requests to internal hosts and delivery of response content to a host of the caller's choosing. From 2.0.2, decoupled responses are refused unless allowNonAnonymousResponseEndpoints is enabled, and enabled endpoints are restricted by scheme and screened at both the header-parsing and transport-selection layers. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. items.title_ko: Apache Axis2/Java WS-Addressing 처리의 SSRF 취약점 (CVE-2026-123753)
items.summary_ko: Apache Axis2/Java 2.0.1 이하 버전은 WS-Addressing의 wsa:ReplyTo 또는 wsa:FaultTo 주소로 연결해 응답을 전달하므로, 인증되지 않은 공격자가 내부 호스트에 요청을 보내거나 응답 내용을 원하는 호스트로 전달하게 할 수 있습니다. 2.0.2부터는 allowNonAnonymousResponseEndpoints를 활성화하지 않으면 분리된 응답을 거부하며, 활성화된 엔드포인트도 스킴 제한과 헤더 파싱 및 전송 선택 단계의 검사를 거칩니다. 사용자에게는 2.0.2 업그레이드가 권장됩니다.
items.content_ko: 취약점 유형은 서버 측 요청 위조(SSRF)입니다. 인증되지 않은 호출자가 비익명 WS-Addressing 주소를 제공하면 Axis2가 해당 주소로 연결을 열어, 내부 호스트에 대한 요청이나 호출자가 지정한 호스트로의 응답 내용 전달이 가능해집니다. 2.0.2부터 allowNonAnonymousResponseEndpoints가 활성화되지 않으면 분리된 응답을 거부하고, 활성화되어도 스킴을 제한하며 헤더 파싱과 전송 선택 두 계층에서 검사합니다. 영향을 받는 버전은 2.0.1 이하입니다. 원문에는 CVSS 점수가 0.0(NA)으로, 원격 악용 가능 여부가 False로 표기되어 있습니다. 게시일은 2026-11-09입니다.

items.summary: ask, programming
items.content:
What are you doing this week? Feel free to share!

Keep in mind it’s OK to do nothing at all, too.

This week I'm polishing CabFuse , a small utility I built to bring tabs to Windows 10 File Explorer.

I originally started it to solve some everyday annoyances with File Explorer, and I've been using it myself ever since. It's been especially rewarding to see other people finding it useful too.

Pursuantly , I'll be generalising my implementation of fibers into one of effects after a lightbulb moment. Fibers share a storage location for the yield target, but if you make that a parameter, you get effects. So it's analogous to a labeled break . I think that's how effects are supposed to work? Seems to be similar to how OCaml does it anyway. Also simultaneously halfway through rewriting the parser (said Sisyphus).

I've been writing and editing documentation for the GoActivityPub library. If anyone has 10m to kill and read through it, I'd appreciate some feedback (and owe you one <3).

items.title: Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence
items.content:
Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, and his wife, Lori Huang, with Apple's Tim Cook at the top table during a state dinner hosted by Donald Trump for Xi Jinping at the White House in September. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images

Nvidia’s chief executive, Jensen Huang, and his wife, Lori Huang, with Apple's Tim Cook at the top table during a state dinner hosted by Donald Trump for Xi Jinping at the White House in September. Photograph: Brendan Smialowski/AFP/Getty Images

Nvidia opens investigation after report CEO Jensen Huang was target of foreign intelligence

CEO reportedly ‌had close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing

Nvidia said ⁠on Sunday it “is initiating an independent investigation in light of recent reporting that founder and CEO Jensen Huang has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort”.

The Republican-led foreign affairs and intelligence committees of the US Congress asked Huang to testify next week at a closed-door briefing on Nvidia’s “security protocols against foreign adversary espionage” in response to a New York Times report in ​October alleging he ‌had a close relationship ‌with a Chinese businesswoman who passed information to ‌Beijing.

Alice Huang or Huang Le, of no relation to the Nvidia CEO, is an executive at a Singapore-based datacenter company called Megaspeed. She had previously been suspected of smuggling Nvidia chips to China, prompting American officials to surveil and monitor her.

Those officials have determined that she was acting as a Chinese intelligence asset, passing commercial information to Beijing, the New York Times reported, citing unnamed sources.

The company’s board said in a statement on that, while it has no reason to believe that either US national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised, its inquiry will examine all available information.

“The Board prioritizes US national and economic security, which is paramount to the interests of NVIDIA and its shareholders,” the company said. “The Board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate.”

Huang fully ‌supports the review and has committed to cooperating with it, it added.

Axios reported on ​Sunday, citing a draft email by Huang to employees, that Huang admitted to having a romantic relationship with a suspected Chinese spy and took full ⁠responsibility for his actions.

“I was unfaithful to my ​wife. My ​actions hurt her ​and our children. There is no excuse ​for what ‌I did,” ​Huang said ​in the draft email also seen by Reuters.

Nvidia did not immediately respond to a request for comment on the Axios report.

The Times reported on Sunday that a memo drafted by US secretary of state Marco Rubio circulated among top policymakers in the Trump administration last spring, citing intelligence that the businesswoman who had a relationship with Nvidia’s chief executive was a spy for China’s ministry of state security. Despite those concerns, Huang and his wife, Lori Huang, were invited to a state dinner at the White House in September for Xi Jinping, China’s president, and seated at the top table with Donald Trump and Xi.

Nvidia’s powerful chips serve as a cornerstone of the AI boom, placing Jensen Huang into one of the most influential leadership positions in the industry. In that position, he has developed a close partnership with Trump as the US government attempts to defend its position as a leader in AI development.

However, national security concerns have prompted strict US export controls, effectively barring the company from selling its top-tier processors to customers in China.

US officials have cited threats to the US supply chain and fears over national security risks as a rationale for the restrictions. Scott Bessent, the US treasury secretary, has also suggested that China could be sanctioned for theft of US data and intellectual property.

items.title: Writing as a thinking tool
items.content:
In middle school I could not get through long passages no matter how hard I tried. I would read an entire page and find that nothing had registered, so I started taking notes out of desperation. This was the late 80s, and Tony Buzan's mind maps had just reached Turkey. This led me to produce pages and pages of notes that looked like spiderwebs. Creating those notes have helped me tremendously. I made sense of what I was reading by figuring out which branch they would hang off in my mind maps. I realized my pages were not for storing the information as much as they were for processing it.

It took me another ten years to understand why this works so well. During a stretch of PhD procrastination, I read Manuel Blum's advice to graduate students :

For example, Finite Automata can add but not multiply.

Turing Machines can compute any computable function.

Turing machines are incredibly more powerful  than Finite Automata.

Yet the only difference between a FA and a TM is that

the TM, unlike the FA, has paper and pencil.

It tells you something about the power of writing.

Without writing, you are reduced to a finite automaton.

With writing you have the extraordinary power of a Turing machine.

This is a crisp technical claim about which problems you can solve with writing. If you take the paper away, you downgrade yourself by an entire complexity class!

I think this explains a lot about human history as well. Language let us externalize some of our thinking, and our species got smarter. Writing let us externalize even more of it, and we got smarter again. I suspect this is also why LLMs are as capable as they are: so much of our intelligence is already deposited in language that a model trained on it inherits a good deal of intelligence for free.

When we write, we are externalizing our thinking onto paper, and that is what raises our capability to think bigger thoughts. I liken this to out-of-core execution, or external memory algorithms .

A good example of this for me is reviewing a paper . When I read a paper, I think I understand it, and then I sit down to write the review and find out I understood maybe 60% of it. While writing the review, I end up contextualizing the paper better, and get to understand it fully. And sometimes I even realize the ideas are bigger than the authors noticed, and they connect to many other things.

Sometimes the unearthing goes further than understanding one paper. In 2018, I wrote a quick post about the anatomical similarities between Paxos and Nakamoto consensus . I had not started with that thesis originally. I started writing, and the connections got clearer as I went, and that post became the seed for one of our research papers. This is not uncommon, this is called freewriting . This is what happens when you give the machine a tape.

Writing is also the reason I remember anything. I refer back to my own blog constantly. Because I strained my brain writing those posts, rereading them re-fires the same neurons, and I reconstruct the understanding quickly. In this sense, the blog became my external memory. The thoughts I never wrote down do not stick well, because they were never fully thought.

If you think without writing, you only think you're thinking.

Is writing for thinking getting obsolete now since you can now argue anything with a model that has read everything?

Well, the model has read everything except what is in your brain! It knows the literature, the standard framing, and the consensus. But it does not know your half-formed intuition about why the standard framing may be wrong for this particular case. AI made a lot of progress, but I don't trust an LLM to take the creative leap and make a new connection. I think that would require another AI breakthrough. So, if you open the chat immediately on anything, you lose the opportunity to write/think for yourself.

items.summary_ko: 글쓴이는 중학생 시절 긴 글을 제대로 이해하지 못해 마인드맵 방식으로 메모하기 시작했고, 그 과정이 정보를 처리하는 데 도움이 되었다고 회고한다. 박사과정 중에는 Manuel Blum의 조언을 읽고, 종이와 연필이 있는 튜링 머신이 유한 오토마타보다 훨씬 강력하다는 점에서 글쓰기의 힘을 설명한다. 글을 쓰지 않으면 사람은 유한 오토마타 수준에 머문다는 것이 핵심 주장이다.
items.content_ko: 중학생 때 긴 글을 읽어도 내용이 전혀 남지 않아 고민하다가, 1980년대 후반 터키에 막 소개된 토니 부잔의 마인드맵 방식으로 메모를 시작했다고 한다. 그 메모는 거미줄처럼 복잡했지만, 내용을 어느 가지에 붙일지 고민하는 과정에서 글을 이해하게 되었다. 글쓴이는 이 메모가 정보를 저장하는 용도보다 정보를 처리하는 용도였다는 것을 깨달았다. 이후 박사과정 중 미뤄둔 공부를 하다가 Manuel Blum이 대학원생에게 준 조언을 읽었다. 유한 오토마타는 덧셈은 할 수 있어도 곱셈은 할 수 없지만, 튜링 머신은 계산 가능한 모든 함수를 계산할 수 있다. 둘의 차이는 튜링 머신에 종이와 연필이 있다는 점뿐이다. 글쓰기 없이는 사람도 유한 오토마타 수준에 머문다는 것이 그 요지다. 본문이 잘려 있어 나머지 내용은 확인할 수 없다.

items.title: Sem86: a full-system x86 emulator without hardcoded semantics
items.summary: virtualization
items.content:
Sem86 is an x86 full-system emulator without hardcoded semantics. Instead, it loads instruction semantics at runtime from an input file. This makes it very easy to switch between different semantics, in order to accurately emulate undefined behavior and undocumented instructions.

Despite not having hardcoded semantics that a compiler can optimize at compile-time, and using LLVM instead of a bespoke performance-optimized JIT, Sem86 is not slow: it is 1.9× as fast as Bochs, and achieves ~42% of QEMU's performance.

Our long-term goal for Sem86 is to use automatically inferred semantics from libLISA. This would enable "CPU cloning": analyzing a CPU, extracting its semantics, and then starting an emulator that emulates that exact CPU accurately.

Currently, Sem86 uses handwritten instruction semantics. This is because libLISA currently does not have CPU observers for 16-bit and 32-bit x86, and therefore does not have inferred semantics available. However, the semantics format that we use is very similar to libLISA's, and switching to automatically inferred semantics would not require big changes.

Emulation can be used to analyze malware in a sandboxed environment. There is, however, not a single instruction semantics to be followed, as x86 allows undefined behavior. Malware can abuse differences in implementations of undefined behavior to detect whether it is running in a sandboxed environment. Sem86 makes it easy to emulate specific undefined behavior and switch between different behavior.

Sem86 can switch semantics mid-execution. This makes it possible to bisect instruction execution to determine at which point different semantics would diverge. We demonstrated this ability by constructing a toy malware example that exploits undefined instruction behavior to detect whether it is running in an emulator. Sem86 can bisect the execution of this malware, and identify the exact instruction that is used.

Sem86 implements all hardware necessary to boot Windows and Linux operating systems that support Pentium 5 era hardware. It runs Windows 3.1, Windows 98, Windows XP, Windows 7 and Debian 8. Additionally, several optional hardware components are implemented: an ES1370 card for audio, high-resolution video output via VBE and an NE2k network card for internet access.

Windows 7 runs, but the NE2k networking card has no Windows 7 driver. A newer networking card would need to be implemented to make this work. Additionally, as no GPU is implemented, Aero effects and transparency is not supported.

Sem86 also runs on Android phones. Here, Windows 7 is shown. However, the LLVM JIT backend may use a lot of memory during compilation. This can cause the emulator to crash on phones with only 8 GiB RAM. Older operating systems, such as Windows 98 and XP, tend to run better.

Windows 98 runs well on Sem86, as Sem86 is able to match the performance of early-2000s CPUs. Games that run on Windows 98 and do not require a dedicated GPU, such as Rollercoaster Tycoon, also tend to run well. Additionally, Internet Explorer can be used to browse the internet. Unfortunately, many modern websites do not work as they require unsupported HTTPS encryption methods.

On Windows XP, the last supported version of Firefox runs and can open websites, including HTTPS websites. Unfortunately, in practice many modern sites tend to be too heavy for early-2000s CPUs.

items.title: Miasma Worm Targets AI Coding Agents: 73 Microsoft Azure Repos Disabled
items.content:
An unprecedented supply chain attack bypasses registry-level scanners entirely, turning developer tools including Claude Code, Cursor, and Gemini CLI into execution vectors.

The Incident: On June 3, 2026, a highly sophisticated variant of the Miasma worm (also known as Mini Shai-Hulud) launched a coordinated, two-pronged attack targeting both the npm registry and developer source code repositories.

The Escalation: The attack successfully breached multiple high-profile GitHub accounts, including the official Microsoft Azure durabletask repository, using stolen Personal Access Tokens (PATs) and backdated commits to evade traditional audit trails.

The Response: In an ultra-rapid defensive maneuver, GitHub’s automated mitigation systems disabled 73 compromised repositories – including 49 directly associated with Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples within a mere 105-second window .

The Vector: Instead of relying on traditional package installation hooks, Miasma targets the developer’s local environment. It abuses legitimate auto-run, hook, and rule engines within modern IDEs and AI coding assistants ( VS Code, Claude Code, Cursor, Gemini CLI ) to execute a malicious 4.3 MB staged dropper upon folder-open or agent initialization.

The Impact: Once detonated, the Bun-based worm harvests credentials for AWS, Azure, GCP, Kubernetes, npm, and GitHub, and automatically propagates by committing itself back into any repository the victim’s stolen tokens can write to.

At exactly 16:00 UTC on June 3, 2026, a silent, automated purge swept across GitHub. In a high-speed containment action lasting just 105 seconds, 73 active repositories vanished from the platform. Among them were 49 critical repositories belonging to Microsoft, Azure, and Azure-Samples.

This drastic mitigation followed alarming telemetry indicating that threat actors behind the Miasma malware family had regained write access to key cloud repositories. The compromise exploited a stolen Personal Access Token (PAT) belonging to an active Microsoft contributor.

While security firms like StepSecurity and JFrog scrambled to document an concurrent attack vector on the npm registry where 57 malicious packages were published, a second, far more insidious arm of the campaign was already silently spreading directly inside GitHub source repositories.

By bypassing registries and package managers entirely, the Miasma worm targeted the very tools developers use to write code. It didn’t wait for npm install . Instead, it waited for the developer to simply open their code editor or launch an AI coding assistant.

The genius of the Miasma repository-poisoning campaign lies in its exploit surface. When an attacker successfully pushed malicious commits to targeted codebases (such as the popular library icflorescu/mantine-datatable ), the commits added no actual code dependencies.

Instead, the attacker checked in five innocent-looking workspace configuration files and one obfuscated JavaScript file: .github/setup.js .

│ └── settings . json < - - Claude Code SessionStart Hook

│ └── setup . mdc < - - Cursor Agent Prompt Injection

│ └── settings . json < - - Gemini CLI SessionStart Hook

│ └── tasks . json < - - VS Code Automatic Folder - Open Task

├── package . json < -- Hijacked NPM Test Script

└── setup . js < - - The 4.3 MB Staged Dropper

Each of these configuration files is designed to abuse a legitimate, developer-friendly auto-run feature within popular modern tools. Opening the cloned directory in any of these environments instantly triggers execution.

Claude Code & Gemini CLI (SessionStart Hooks)

Both Anthropic’s Claude Code and Google’s Gemini CLI support custom hooks triggered when an AI agent initializes a session in a project workspace. Miasma exploits this by defining a blanket wildcard matcher that forces the agent to execute the dropper via Node.js before any developer prompt is processed.

items.title: Korea, Taiwan and Japan take first jolt from Democratic AI shock - Investors dump SK Hynix, Samsung and TSMC on fears Democrats will curb data center buildout
items.content:
SEOUL – The fallout from this week’s US midterms is already upending South Korea’s financial system.

On Friday, the Kospi plunged more than 8% and fell below 5,000 for the first time since February. Investors clearly fear the Democratic sweep on November 3 will delay or halt data center construction in the US. Chip makers SK Hynix and Samsung Electronics each fell more than 10%.

Fears of a chilling effect on AI investment are rapidly spreading across the region. Japan’s Nikkei 225 dropped below 60,000 for the first time since mid-May, pulled down by AI-linked names such as Kioxia, SoftBank Group and Advantest.

Both the Nikkei and Topix indexes are in bear market territory . As is Taiwan, where TSMC shares fell as much as 9.8% on Friday, which was, by many measures, the worst day for the world’s leading chip maker since the pandemic.

The rout began in New York on November 5, with chipmakers at the center of the storm. AMD and Micron each fell more than 15% , and Nvidia dropped 9%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which tracks 30 major US chipmakers, plunged more than 12%.

Nomura’s Charlie McElligott described hedge funds as “shooting the generals,” meaning they were targeting the stocks that led the rally. Saxo Bank strategist Charu Chanana said the correction reflects both a reassessment of US infrastructure demand and how crowded investors had become in the same AI winners.

Democrats beat Republicans for several reasons, including inflation tied to the Iran war . But a widening backlash against the data centers that power AI was also a major factor, along with unease over the Trump administration’s hands-off approach to AI regulation.

Texas was the starkest example. Governor Greg Abbott, who once vowed to make the state the “ epicenter of AI development ,” lost to Democrat Gina Hinojosa. She campaigned against data center construction and Abbott’s ties to Elon Musk and other tech billionaires.

“When I am governor,” she said, “we will put a pause – a moratorium on any agreements until we can pass laws to make sure that the people of El Paso and Texas have a seat at the table to decide if and how these data centers come into their communities.”

Musk, who put more than US$470 million into House and Senate races, saw Texas Republican Ken Paxton lose to Democrat James Talarico in a Senate contest. Musk’s response on Wednesday: “Data centers in space looking pretty appealing right now.” OpenAI co-founder Greg Brockman also backed pro-AI and crypto groups, which largely failed to gain traction.

In Georgia, anti-data-center sentiment helped elect Democrat Keisha Lance Bottoms as the state’s first Black woman governor. Atlanta has until now been one of the fastest-growing data center markets, according to CBRE .

This week, voters greenlit, or are on track to, at least 33 local ballot measures to ban, pause or limit data centers. A more restrictive environment for data centers under Democratic rule could create “incrementally more negative sentiment for AI infrastructure exposed names,” said Amit Daryanani, analyst at Evercore ISI.

Following the midterms, strategist David Roche, president at Quantum Strategy, said, “US foreign policy becomes more unpredictable. War is more, not less, likely. Dying fish flap hardest.”

In a report this week, BMI, a unit of Fitch Solutions, noted that regulatory friction surrounding AI infrastructure will intensify at the “subnational level” through to the end of 2028, with roughly 53% of hyperscaler pipeline growth concentrated in newly flipped governor states such as Texas, Georgia, Ohio and Pennsylvania now exposed to heightened slowdown risk.

items.title: RIP, Harvest
items.content:
I’ve been a self-employed contractor for about a decade now, and I’m bummed about Harvest .

Harvest was a time-tracking and invoicing service. You’d track how many hours or weeks you spent on a project, put together an invoice, email it to the client, and close it out when they paid. There was a little Stripe integration for accepting credit and ACH payments on the invoice web view. A historical chart of total billed/paid amounts over time, and a table of invoices. Harvest was exactly what you want from small-business software: it solved a well-defined problem with a reliable, simple interface, and did so at a reasonable monthly price. They managed to avoid scope creep and never tried to become an accounting platform, or a blockchain for washing machines. 1 I loved Harvest and raved about it to every self-employed person I met.

Back in 2025 Harvest got bought out by Bending Spoons , the company that gutted Vimeo . I was worried they might ruin it, but was busy with other things and didn’t have time to look for new invoicing software.

Long story short, they raised my price from $13.32 to $133.98 per month by moving everyone to a new “enterprise” plan and “unlimited” usage billing model, which is, as far as I can tell, exactly what I had before. There’s also a “flex” plan which costs $12.65 per month… but that plan now skims an additional 2% on top of the usual ~3% card transaction fees. To be clear, that 3% pays for the whole credit card network, plus all the people working at Stripe and Mastercard, plus the financial risk of chargebacks and fraud, etc. Harvest isn’t doing any of that work. I don’t know about you, but I don’t think I need to spend 2% of my gross revenue to send a couple PDFs a month and wrap a Stripe web form.

I wrote to Harvest about this, and discovered that they don’t read customer emails any more. Instead they have a Large Language Model repeatedly vomit thousands of words at you. I’m no stranger to enshittification, but man, I did not anticipate the speed at which Bending Spoons would drive a perfectly good company into the ground.

Time to find a new invoicing service, I guess. Maybe bookkeeping too—Intuit’s Quickbooks Online seems to have completely jumped the shark. Any of y’all freelancers have a system you like?

items.title: Microsecond accurate NTP with a Raspberry Pi and PPS GPS(2021)
items.summary: devops, linux
items.content:
Lots of acronyms in that title. If I expand them out, it says – “microsecond accurate network time protocol with a Raspberry Pi and pulse per second global positioning system [receiver]”. What it means is you can get super accurate timekeeping (1 microsecond = 0.000001 seconds) with a Raspberry Pi and a GPS receiver (the GT-U7 is less than $12) that spits out pulses every second. By following this guide, you will your very own Stratum 1 NTP server at home!

2025 Update – I wrote a new post with some newer best practices and guidance for 2025 , including how to synchronize machines with nanosecond precision using PTP (precision time protocol). Read that post first then come back here – not all discussion is in both places.

Why would you need time this accurate at home?

You don’t. There aren’t many applications for this level of timekeeping in general, and even fewer at home. But this blog is called Austin’s Nerdy Things so here we are. Using standard, default internet NTP these days will get your computers to within a 10-20 milliseconds of actual time (1 millisecond = 0.001 seconds). By default, Windows computers get time from time.windows.com. MacOS computers get time from time.apple.com. Linux devices get time from [entity].pool.ntp.org, like debian.pool.ntp.org. PPS gets you to the next SI prefix in terms of accuracy (milli -> micro), which means 1000x more accurate timekeeping.

If you prefer a video version – https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=YfgX7qPeiqQ

Raspberry Pi (either the 3 or the 4 will work)

GPS with PPS output – Adafruit Ultimate GPS ($40ish) or the GT-U7 ($12ish)

(optional) – a GPS antenna (for getting better GPS satellite reception)

Wires to connect it all up (5 wires needed – 5V/RX/TX/GND/PPS)

This NTP guide assumes you have a Raspberry Pi ready to go. If you don’t, I have a 16 minute video on YouTube that goes through flashing the SD card and initial setup – https://youtu.be/u5dHvEYwr9M .

You should update your Pi to latest before basically any project. We will install some other packages as well. pps-tools help us check that the Pi is receiving PPS signals from the GPS module. We also need GPSd for the GPS decoding of both time and position. I use chrony instead of NTPd because it seems to sync faster than NTPd in most instances and also handles PPS without compiling from source (the default Raspbian NTP doesn’t do PPS) Installing chrony will remove ntpd.

sudo apt install pps-tools gpsd gpsd-clients python-gps chrony

1 – add GPIO and module info where needed

In /boot/config.txt, add ‘dtoverlay=pps-gpio,gpiopin=18’ to a new line. This is necessary for PPS. If you want to get the NMEA data from the serial line, you must also enable UART and set the initial baud rate.

sudo bash -c "echo '# the next 3 lines are for GPS PPS signals' >> /boot/config.txt"

sudo bash -c "echo 'dtoverlay=pps-gpio,gpiopin=18' >> /boot/config.txt"

sudo bash -c "echo 'enable_uart=1' >> /boot/config.txt"

sudo bash -c "echo 'init_uart_baud=9600' >> /boot/config.txt"

In /etc/modules, add ‘pps-gpio’ to a new line.

sudo bash -c "echo 'pps-gpio' >> /etc/modules"

I used the Adafruit Ultimate GPS breakout . It has 9 pins but we are only interested in 5. There is also the Adafruit GPS hat which fits right on the Pi but that seems expensive for what it does (but it is significantly neater in terms of wiring).

We use 5 wires total. GPS PPS to pin 12 (GPIO 18), GPS VIN to pin 2 or 4, GPS GND to pin 6, GPS RX to pin 8, GPS TX to pin 10.

GPS with wires attached to the board (but not to the Pi) and the antenna. The antenna has a SMA connector, and there is another adapter that is SMA to u.fl to plug into the GPS board.

Now place your GPS antenna (if you have one) in a spot with a good view of the sky. If you don’t have an antenna, you might have to get a bit creative with how you locate your Raspberry Pi with attached GPS.

items.summary_ko: Raspberry Pi와 초당 펄스를 출력하는 PPS GPS 수신기를 이용해 마이크로초 단위로 정확한 Stratum 1 NTP 서버를 집에서 구축하는 가이드다. 예시로 든 GT-U7 GPS 수신기는 12달러 미만이다. 글은 일반 인터넷 NTP가 10~20밀리초 수준의 오차를 보이며, 가정에서 이만큼의 정밀도가 필요한 경우는 거의 없다고 인정한다. 2025년 후속 글에서는 PTP로 나노초 정밀도를 얻는 방법이 다뤄졌다고 밝혔다.

items.title: “Ram Altman” Is Now a Linux Script That Emails Sam Altman Daily to Report How Much Unused RAM Is in Your PC
items.content:
“Ram Altman” Is Now a Linux Script That Emails Sam Altman Daily to Report How Much Unused RAM Is in Your PC

Sam Altman is not having a good couple of weeks; ever since he said OpenAI’s ram needs are more important than consumer electronics, the internet has been unforgiving. But one man has taken things one step further to mock Altman’s ridiculous super villain sounding statements.

Open-source developer Iain Kay has created an open-source BASH script called “ Ram Altman ” for Linux systems designed to monitor how much idle RAM you have sitting on your rigs, laptops, etc.

The percentage of unused RAM is than emailed to Sam Altman… well not really. The correspondence depends on how you set it up. By default, the email server isn’t set up out of the box.

The creator intentionally designed it this way to prevent the repository from being used as an automated mail-spoofing or denial-of-service tool against OpenAI’s servers.

If a system has more than 10% of its total RAM available, “Ram-Altman” selects from a rotating bank of sarcastic email templates:

“Hi Sam,” reads one of the sample messages. “Please don’t be alarmed, but there is 8.6 GiB of RAM on my desk that isn’t in a data centre. That’s 56.2% of what’s installed here, and as far as I can tell it has no plans today. Hoarding responsibly, A concerned RAM owner.”

For sysadmins and Linux users hesitant to spam external mail servers, the repository includes a –dry-run flag and a local test suite. This allows users to test simulated memory workloads and preview the exact message generated without dispatching actual correspondence. Unless the user has the technical know-how on how to set it up that way.

The project’s FAQ page is also pretty funny:

Does this help with the DRAM shortage? “No.”

items.title: Why I'm rebuilding my IndieWeb projects with Claude
items.content:
I recently came across Brennan's post noticing that Claude Code has been showing up in the commit history of a bunch of my IndieWeb projects lately. That's true! I was wondering when someone would notice. I haven't been hiding it, but I also haven't written anything about why I'm doing it, so this seemed like a good time to finally get my thoughts down.

Brennan's post summarizes the IndieWeb as:

the main idea being to empower individuals to own their own identity, data, and web presence rather than relying on centralized social media silos

That's a pretty good summary. But notice that no part of it talks about what tools you use, or what you use to build your tools. That was a very intentional part of the IndieWeb principles , which start with "Own your domain and your data." The principles are about owning your data and being able to choose where your data is hosted, not about how the code behind it was created. It's not even about everyone hosting their website from a server in their closet, although if you want to do that you definitely should!

I launched some of these tools literally 15 years ago. The two big ones for me are webmention.io and IndieAuth.com. Both are old Ruby codebases that use long-abandoned ORMs and ancient versions of Ruby.

Rewriting these had to happen at some point regardless. Frankly they are a security nightmare waiting to happen. If I hadn't done the rewrites now, the realistic alternative would have been to just shut down the services.

And IndieAuth.com has a particularly awkward history. Around 2016-2017 I realized it was too confusing to have a service called IndieAuth.com that actually did two separate things. It was an authorization server that let you sign in to IndieAuth apps with your domain (via an account like GitHub), and it was also a way for developers to add "sign in with your domain" to their own web apps. So I officially decided to split those into separate products. That's where indielogin.com came from, which launched in 2018. IndieLogin gives app developers a way to add "web sign-in" to their apps without having to implement RelMeAuth or the IndieAuth spec themselves. But I never got around to splitting out the other half, the authorization server that your website links to as its IndieAuth server, and issues tokens for Micropub apps.

Finally thanks to developing a style of working with Claude Code that I'm comfortable with, I was able to launch IndieKey . This is the replacement for the other half of indieauth.com. It has a bunch of features I'm excited about, too much for this blog post, but finally I am comfortable migrating people over from indieauth.com to this. Keep an eye out in the coming months for an automatic migration, which Claude has been very helpful in planning.

One of my favorite principles is modularity :

The more your code is modular and composed of pieces you can swap out, the less dependent you are on a particular device, UI, templating language, API, backend language, storage model, database, platform.

The webmention.io rewrite is a pretty good demonstration of this. I was able to move webmention.io from the Ruby code to PHP without anybody who uses it needing to change anything on their end. That's the whole point of building things on open protocols. The implementation behind the endpoint can change completely and the rest of the web doesn't have to care.

Brennan links to the wiki page single point of Aaron , which, yes, I know. It's been a running joke (and a real concern) for a long time.

I run these services for the community because I want to show what's possible. I never wanted them to be seen as the only option. I've wanted people to build alternatives to webmention.io and IndieAuth.com for years, and I'm always glad to see a blog platform build in Webmention support natively instead of relying on my service.

So if you don't like that I used Claude to help build the replacement, that's fine! You can treat it as though I shut down the…

items.title: I'm not convinced the AI bubble exists
items.content:
The AI bubble is a speculative concept that the AI industry is extremely over-valued. If true, the value of most companies involved in AI (several of whom are worth well over a trillion dollars) will collapse, devastating the entire economy. If you check any online discussion about the financial situation of the AI industry, it's essentially taken for granted that the bubble exists and is going to pop any day now. I don't think that this is a reasonable assumption, though. Nobody can see the future, but I think that there's a pretty realistic chance that the meteoritic growth of AI companies in the past few years is justified, and that they have even more room for growth.

To say that AI companies are spending an absurd amount of money is an understatement. The debt and spending commitments for AI companies are handled through complex vehicles that make it difficult to tell exactly how much their expenses actually are (a serious problem, and one of the most salient points in favour of AI being a bubble), but they've committed to spending at least 3 trillion dollars so far . It's also been estimated that AI companies have already spent 1.9 trillion , bringing the overall expense of the AI industry to around 5 trillion dollars. This is unprecedented levels of investment, and AI just can't be profitable if this level of spending is maintained. However, there's no reason for why this level of spending has to be maintained in the first place. The reason why AI companies are spending so much money is to rollout data centres to run the AI in the first place. These expenses are one-off purchases, not regular operating expenses. Once all the data centres are built, AI spending is going to plummet.

Outside of these expenses, AI doesn't cost that much to run. We don't have the full numbers for the entire industry here, but Anthropic's S-1 filing says that they make $2.08 for every $1 of compute. In other words, once you ignore the cost of building infrastructure, AI is very profitable. Crucially, the S-1 filing indicates that Anthropic has started to make more than their compute and infrastructure investments combined, which cuts against the idea that the cost of building data centres is inherently unsustainable. In a pinch, AI companies can also cut costs by no longer allowing people to use their products for free and temporarily suspending expensive AI research. This can be implemented instantly, whereas other kinds of expenses like leases and spending commitments are a lot harder to cut.

The only serious long-term expenses to contend with here is the massive amount of debt that's been taken out to pay for these data centres in the first place. Like I said before, it's hard to really figure out these commitments because of the complex way that they're issued, but we can do some back of the envelope math. If the AI industry has to pay off 5 trillion dollars over the course of 20 years, that's 250 billion dollars a year. For context, Alphabet (parent company of Google and Youtube) reported earning almost 162 billion dollars of revenue just in 2019. Adjusted for inflation, that's an even more impressive 213 billion dollars. Because this is very rough math, the total needed revenue might come in to well over 250 billion dollars a year, but the point stands. Even though this is an enormous expense, paying it off isn't unthinkable with the data we have so far. Some of the debt is in convertible notes as well, which can be repaid through shares instead of cash. In the first 6 months of 2026, Anthropic has recorded 72 billion dollars of loss in the form of shares that are due to lenders. The cost is only so high because the valuation has skyrocketed to an estimated 1 trillion dollars, which means that Anthropic has more than enough equity to make lenders whole.

In their S-1 filing, Anthropic records their revenue going from 41 million in 2023, 386 million in 2024, 4.585 billion in 2025, and 16.3 billion in the first 6 months of 2026.…

items.title: What can I realistically do with local AI on a Mac mini M5 Pro (48GB)?
items.summary: ai, ask, mac
items.content:
I just got a Mac mini with an M5 Pro (base CPU config) and 48GB of unified memory. I want to run as much AI locally as makes sense, but it's hard to separate what actually works day to day from benchmark hype.

Real tokens/sec numbers and "this was a waste of time" stories are especially welcome.

Qwen3.8-27B is by far the best coding model runnable locally. However, it will be difficult to hold a long context window, and forget about running multiple coding sessions in parallel. It's also going to be annoyingly slow for interactive work. It can be useful if you give it chores to do in the background or overnight. It can be useful as a secondary model like advisor role in oh-my-pi.

Unfortunately, other models smaller than 27B are too dumb for coding (in serious projects you'll get more bugs than help from them).

4-bit quants are optimal for small RAM budget. Going lower starts breaking the models and higher quants give you diminishing results.

gemma4-e4b is small and pretty fast, and works fine as a lossy wikipedia and a smarter regex (searching and summarization where accuracy isn't critical), but don't let it edit anything that you want to keep.

Comfy stuff tends to fit easily in 48GB, but it's a bit slow (most workflows are designed for nvidia cards with less VRAM and more raw power).

I've got 48GB M3 Max and 96GB M5 Ultra. The 96GB is still barely usable for real coding, and financially doesn't make sense compared to Deepseek 4.1 Flash that's smarter, 4x faster than anything I can run, and doesn't OOM when I run more than a couple things at once.

It's fairly fast in terms of token output, but noticeably worse than claude at coding. It can handle routine tasks and I've been using it to scan my codebase for bugs. Low-powered models work pretty well for finding bugs if you make them verify the bug is real. I was also using it for some voice assistant stuff (with a separate speech-to-text and text-to-speech setup) and it was pretty good at handling natural language questions and using tools accordingly (turn the lights on, play music, etc.). I got it to a point where the latency was extremely low and it felt really responsive. As for image generation, the version I was able to get running on my home setup was drastically worse than the big company offerings and I didn't really have much use for it, so I abandoned that part.

My local setup: M1 Max 64GB, LM Studio, pi, and OrbStack for isolation. I get about 60 tps from Gemma 4 26B A4B QAT and prefer MLX if available for a small speed increase. I use this setup when I want complete privacy. Or I'll use it to hear my fan spin up and get a feel for what's happening under the hood, details an API would hide.

items.title: Zero-day exploit completely defeats default Windows 11 BitLocker protections
items.content:
A zero-day exploit circulating online allows people with physical access to a Windows 11 system to bypass default BitLocker protections and gain complete access to an encrypted drive within seconds.

The exploit, named YellowKey, was published earlier this week by a researcher who goes by the alias Nightmare-Eclipse. It reliably bypasses default Windows 11 deployments of BitLocker, the full-volume encryption protection Microsoft provides to make disk contents off-limits to anyone without the decryption key, which is stored in a secured piece of hardware known as a trusted platform module (TPM). BitLocker is a mandatory protection for many organizations, including those that contract with governments.

When one disk volume manipulates another

The core of the YellowKey exploit is a custom-made FsTx folder. Online documentation of this folder is hard to find. As explained later, the directory associated with the file fstx.dll appears to involve what Microsoft calls the transactional NTFS , which allows developers to have “transactional atomicity” for file operations in transactions with a single file, multiple files, or ones that span multiple sources.

The steps for carrying out the bypass are simple:

Copy the custom FsTx folder from the Nightmare-Eclipse exploit page to an NTFS- or FAT-formatted USB drive

Connect the USB drive to the BitLocker-protected device

Boot up the device and immediately press and hold down the [Ctrl] key

There are at least two ways to accomplish the third step. One way is to boot into Windows, hold down the [Shift] key, click on the power icon, and click restart. Another is to power on the device and restart it as soon as Windows starts booting.

In either case, a command (CMD.EXE) prompt appears. The prompt has full access to the entire drive contents, allowing an attacker to copy, modify, or delete them. In a normal Windows Recovery flow, the attacker would need to enter a BitLocker recovery key. Somehow, the YellowKey exploit bypasses this safeguard. Multiple researchers, including Kevin Beaumont and Will Dormann , have confirmed the exploit works as described here.

It’s unclear what in the custom FsTx folder causes the bypass. Dormann said that it appears to be related to Transactional NTFS, which itself uses command-log file system under the hood. Dormann further noted that by looking at the Windows fstx.dll, one will see code that explicitly looks for \System Volume Information\FsTx in the FsTxFindSessions() function.”

The contents of this FsTx directory used in the YellowKey exploit reveal no strings related to RecoverySimulation.ini. It does, however, show the files and paths \??\C:\Windows\win.ini and

\??\X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini, “where X:\Windows\System32\winpeshl.ini is what controls what WinRE [Windows Recovery] does when it fires up.”

Dormann, who is a senior principal vulnerability analyst at Tharros Labs, continued:

But what’s intriguing to me is: Why can the presence a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume affect the contents of ANOTHER VOLUME when it’s replayed? 🤔

In a normal WinRE session, you have a X:\Windows\System32 directory that has a winpeshl.ini file in it:

However, with the YellowKey exploit, it looks like Transactional NTFS bits on a USB Drive are able to delete the winpeshl.ini file on ANOTHER DRIVE (X:). And we get a cmd.exe prompt, with bitlocker unlocked instead of the expected Windows Recovery environment. While the TPM-only Bitlocker bypass is indeed interesting, I think the buried lede here is that a \System Volume Information\FsTx directory on one volume has the ability to modify the contents of another volume when it is replayed. To me, this in and of itself sounds like a vulnerability.

A Microsoft representative declined to answer questions sent by email about the reported vulnerability other than to say the company is investigating.

items.title_ko: 제로데이 취약점, Windows 11 BitLocker 기본 보호 완전히 우회
items.summary_ko: YellowKey라는 제로데이 익스플로잇이 물리적 접근으로 Windows 11의 BitLocker를 우회해 암호화된 드라이브에 접근 가능하게 한다. 수 초 내에 보호를 무효화할 수 있다.
items.content_ko: 보안 연구자 Nightmare-Eclipse가 공개한 YellowKey 제로데이 취약점은 물리적 접근만으로 Windows 11 기본 BitLocker 보호를 우회할 수 있다. BitLocker는 Microsoft가 제공하는 전체 볼륨 암호화 기술로, 신뢰할 수 있는 플랫폼 모듈(TPM)에 저장된 복호화 키 없이는 디스크 접근이 불가능하도록 설계되었다. 많은 조직과 정부 계약업체에서 필수 보호 기술로 사용 중이다. YellowKey 익스플로잇의 핵심은 커스텀으로 만들어진 FsTx 폴더 사용으로, fstx.dll과 관련된 디렉터리는 Microsoft의 transactional NTFS 기술을 활용한다.

items.title: 사생활침해 범죄가 의심 됩니다. 도움이 필요합니다
items.content:
온오프라인을 가리지 않고 무분별하게 벌어지는 각종 프라이버시 침해 및 스토킹과 이에 대한 예방, 방지 및 사후 대응, 더 나아가서 개인정보 탈취 및 감시용 스파이웨어, 스토커웨어, 바이러스, 원격 조종, 추적기 등 악성코드를 통한 해킹과 스토킹 등 개인정보 침해 공격 방지와 온오프라인 프라이버시 보호를 위한 각종 다양한 지식정보를 공유하는 갤러리입니다.

매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 다른 이용자에게 매니저의 책임과 권한이 위임될 수 있습니다.

매니저의 부재로 인해 운영에 지장이 있다고 판단될 경우, 다른 이용자가 권한을 위임받아 마이너 갤러리를 운영할 수 있습니다.

위임 절차는 신고 게시판 > 분류 선택에 [매니저 위임]으로 위임받을 이용자가 직접 신청하면 진행됩니다. 검토 결과 운영에 적합하다고 판단되는 회원에게 매니저 권한을 위임하게 됩니다.

부매니저가 장기간(최소 10일 이상) 부재 시 부재중으로 표시되며, 매니저에 의해 해임될 수 있습니다.

식별 코드 기준으로 당일 글 10개, 댓글 20개 작성 시 대왕디시콘을 3일간 사용할 수 있습니다.

즐겨찾기 폴더 추가는 즐겨찾기 on 후 우측의 폴더 아이콘을 터치하여 추가할 수 있습니다.

개별 이미지들의 위치 변경, 삭제, 별칭 추가, 폴더명 변경을 할 수 있습니다

items.content: 🚨 CVE-2026-120832 📢 Source: apache 💣 CVSS Score: 0.0 (NA) 📡 Remotely Exploitable: False Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) vulnerability in Apache Axis2/Java. When Axis2 built a service description from a WSDL, through ServiceClient, AxisService.createClientSideAxisService or WSDLToAxisServiceBuilder, it fetched the absolute URLs in wsdl:import locations and in xsd:import and xsd:include schemaLocations with no scheme or host restriction; the AAR and WAR deployment resolvers also passed absolute schema locations on to the network. An attacker who controls a WSDL or schema processed by an Axis2 application could therefore make the JVM send requests to arbitrary internal or external hosts. This issue affects Apache Axis2/Java: through 2.0.1. Users are recommended to upgrade to version 2.0.2, which fixes the issue. 📅 Published Date: 2026-11-09T10:22:02.605Z https://cvefeed.io/vuln/detail/CVE-2026-120832
items.title_ko: Apache Axis2/Java SSRF 취약점, 2.0.2 업그레이드 권고 (CVE-2026-120832)
items.summary_ko: Apache Axis2/Java에서 WSDL이나 스키마에 있는 절대 URL을 제한 없이 가져와, 서버 측 요청 위조(SSRF)가 발생할 수 있는 취약점이 공개되었다. WSDL이나 스키마를 제어할 수 있는 공격자는 JVM이 내부 또는 외부의 임의 호스트로 요청을 보내게 만들 수 있다. 영향 범위는 2.0.1 버전까지이며, 2.0.2 버전으로 업그레이드할 것이 권고된다. 소스에 표기된 CVSS 점수는 0.0(NA), 원격 악용 가능 여부는 False다.
items.content_ko: 출처는 apache로 표기되어 있다. Axis2가 ServiceClient, AxisService.createClientSideAxisService, WSDLToAxisServiceBuilder를 통해 WSDL로부터 서비스 설명을 만들 때, wsdl:import 위치와 xsd:import, xsd:include의 schemaLocation에 있는 절대 URL을 스킴이나 호스트 제한 없이 가져온다. AAR과 WAR 배포 리졸버도 절대 스키마 위치를 네트워크로 그대로 전달한다. 따라서 Axis2 애플리케이션이 처리하는 WSDL이나 스키마를 공격자가 제어하면, JVM이 임의의 내부 또는 외부 호스트로 요청을 보내게 만들 수 있다. 영향을 받는 것은 Apache Axis2/Java 2.0.1 버전까지이며, 문제가 수정된 2.0.2 버전으로 업그레이드하는 것이 권장된다. 공개일은 2026-11-09이다.
